_comment: Accepted divergences for the goip <-> ip netlink parity comparator.
Reviewed like docs/coverage-baseline.txt and like
nix/checks/proto-audit-netlink-allowlist.json: an entry is a standing
decision, so adding one needs the same scrutiny as lowering a coverage
floor. A divergence that is merely inconvenient does not belong here - only
one that is correct.
AN ENTRY SUPPRESSES A VALUE, NEVER A PRESENCE. The loader enforces this in
code (Allowlist.Suppresses refuses every class but DivergenceValue) rather
than trusting the rule to be remembered, because the failure mode is
silent: a goip that omits an attribute entirely would be masked by that
attribute's VALUE being noisy, and the resulting report would look clean.
Transaction counts, key-set membership, key ordering and attribute-type
ordering are therefore unsuppressible by construction.
A locus is spelled the way the comparator DERIVES it, never the way a
human would name the same thing. A request locus ends in `dump` or `get`
because NLM_F_DUMP is the only thing on the wire that separates iproute2's
ll_init_map from its ll_link_get, and a comparator cannot see a C function
name. The call site belongs in `reason`, where prose belongs; an entry
whose locus is prose is an entry that matches nothing.
Entries are matched on command + locus, and the locus names the thing being
asserted. That is the same discipline as the proto-audit allowlist keying on
wire bit offset: a divergence that MOVES stops being allowlisted and the
check goes red again. Two entries sharing a locus is an error, not a
precedence rule, because nothing would say which one applied.
FOUR KINDS:
kind=version-skew   the pinned `ip` and a different `ip` release disagree,
so the divergence is a property of the target rather
than of goip. MUST carry ip_version: the entry is a
statement about one release, and it has to stop
applying when the pin moves.
kind=side-socket    traffic from a socket that is not the tool's own.
Advisory topologies only - the clean capture namespace
emits none, which is why it is the gated one.
kind=volatile-fallback  a value that moved between the two control
captures. Every one of these is a bug report against
D_control, not a resting place: a noisy control means
distrust the run.
kind=accepted-divergence  goip is deliberately different and will stay
different. Needs the argument in `reason`.
gated_commands mirrors nix/checks/default.nix's gate-one-at-a-time
discipline. A command joins only once its entries have reasons AND a live
Tier C run has been observed clean for it - not optimistically, and not on
the strength of the hermetic tiers, which compare recorded bytes and so
cannot tell you what today's kernel does.
`link show` was the first member, and what it rested on is one
measurement: `nix run .#microvm-x86_64-goip-parity` reported
GOIP_PARITY_PASS link_show with `control: nl=0 stdout=0` - one transaction
each side, no divergence at any level, and nothing suppressed, not even
this file's own stdout:keyword:qlen entry, because the clean namespace has
no link with IFLA_TXQLEN = 0 for it to fire on. That last part matters: an
entry that does not fire is not evidence that it is unnecessary, only that
this topology does not reach it.
`link show dev`, `route show`, `route show table all` and `-6 route show`
joined on the same bar and nothing weaker. Each reported GOIP_PARITY_PASS
with `control: nl=0 stdout=0` and NO findings at all - not suppressed ones,
none - on two consecutive Tier C runs whose every line was identical,
transaction counts included: `link show dev` 2/2, `route show` 2/2, `route
show table all` 3/3, `-6 route show` 2/2. Two runs rather than one is the
CONTROL_NOISY lesson applied: a single run cannot tell a property from a
sample. The one divergence these carry is invisible to the comparator by
design - `ll_link_get` opens a throwaway socket per lookup while goip
reuses its fd, so the `pids` column differs - and nlmsg_pid is normalized
before any byte is compared.
`link show dev` also carries a dormant version-skew entry below. A dormant
entry is not a reason to hold a command back: it does not fire at the
7.1.0 pin, so gating changes nothing today. What it changes is that after a
nixpkgs bump past de91e928 the entry is what keeps the command green
instead of merely quiet. That is the entire practical delta of gating it.
`addr show`, `-4 addr show`, `-6 addr show` and `neigh show` complete the
table, and they are the interesting four, because two of them are the
CONTROL_NOISY ones. Their four loci are IFLA_STATS and IFLA_STATS64 on
ifindex 2 in txn[0] of `-4 addr show` and of `neigh show`: the kernel
appends live packet and byte counters, which move between the two control
captures by construction - one measured run has rx_packets = 0x81 on ip_a
and 0x8a on goip, sixty milliseconds of traffic apart.
Both of those link dumps lack RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS, but NOT for the
same reason, and the difference decides which of them can ever stop being
noisy. `-4 addr show`'s dump carries no IFLA_EXT_MASK at all - 32 bytes,
ifi_family = AF_INET, no attribute - because rtnl_linkdump_req_filter_fn
forwards filter_fn only for AF_UNSPEC and AF_PACKET (lib/libnetlink.c:595).
`neigh show`'s dump DOES carry one, and its value is 0x01: 40 bytes, with
0800 1d00 01000000 at offset 0x58 of netlink_route_getneigh.pcap, which is
ll_init_map's RTEXT_FILTER_VF. This paragraph used to say neither carried
the attribute, which was true of the first and false of the second. Same
absent bit, two mechanisms, and only the second is one an iproute2 bump
moves - see the version-skew entries below, and what they now say about
the reply side.
Gating them anyway is correct, and the reason is a distinction worth
stating rather than trusting. A control-suppressed locus is not a finding.
D_control absorbs it before Result.Findings is built, which is why those
commands report `control: nl=2 stdout=0` next to GOIP_PARITY_PASS and not
WARN - and Report.Failed is `Gated && len(Findings) != 0`, so a gate has
nothing to act on. CONTROL_NOISY is advisory and never touches the verdict
(internal/goipparity/compare.go:324-328). Gating a noisy command therefore
changes its verdict in exactly one situation: a divergence D_control could
NOT explain. That is the situation worth failing on, and it is the only one
these four now fail on.
For the interval in which these nine WERE the whole table,
GOIP_PARITY_UNGATED_CLEAN was vacuously true: it counts StatusWarn on
commands outside this list, and there were none left. That interval is
over. `-s link show` is the tenth command and is deliberately ungated -
its replies carry live counters, so it is expected to be permanently
CONTROL_NOISY, and it must be MEASURED noisy before anyone decides what
that means. UNGATED_CLEAN is therefore load-bearing again.
`-4 link show` and `-6 link show` are the eleventh and twelfth commands
and they are gated, on their own two runs and not on the argument that
they must be identical to `link show`. The argument is a good one -
ipaddr_list_link overwrites preferred_family with AF_PACKET before it
parses an argument (ip/ipaddress.c:2416), so all three forms build the
same request - but it is the thing being tested, so it cannot also be
the reason for not testing it. Both reported `control: nl=0 stdout=0`
with one transaction each side and nothing suppressed, twice, which is
the same bar `link show` cleared.
`addr show dev` is the thirteenth and it is gated, on two measured runs
whose GOIP_PARITY lines were byte-identical to each other. Both reported
`txns: ip=3 goip=3` and `control: nl=0 stdout=0` with nothing suppressed
- not even a suppressed finding - which is the bar this file sets at the
top and the same one `link show` cleared. All three sides captured seven
datagrams and 567 bytes of stdout. The ip side shows two pids to goip's
one, because ll_link_get opens a throwaway socket, exactly as
`link show dev` does.
Gating it matters more than two clean runs suggest, because two of its
three requests are invisible to any output comparison. Request one is by
NAME with ifi_family AF_UNSPEC and request two is by INDEX with
ifi_family = filter.family; on a plain `addr show dev` both of those
bytes are 0, for two unrelated reasons. A goip that sent either request
twice, or that swapped them, would print byte-identical text. Only the
gate turns that into a failure.
`route show dev` is the fourteenth and it is gated, on two measured runs
whose GOIP_PARITY lines were byte-identical. Both reported `txns: ip=2
goip=2` and `control: nl=0 stdout=0` with nothing suppressed, five
datagrams and 302 bytes of stdout on all three sides.
Gating it buys something no other row does, because this selector makes
the command CHEAPER and the saving is invisible to every count. `route
show` and `route show dev` both measure five datagrams and ten messages
on this topology, and they are not the same five. `route show` sends the
dump first and then one lazy RTM_GETLINK at the END, BY INDEX, to name
the interface each route prints. `route show dev` sends an RTM_GETLINK
FIRST, BY NAME, to resolve the selector - and then none at all, because
print_route's `dev` token is guarded on `filter.oifmask != -1`
(ip/iproute.c:900-901) and that token is the only caller of
ll_index_to_name for RTA_OIF. The get moved from the back to the front
and changed shape, and the transaction count did not move. Only
positional request equality can see that.
Its dump is also the only RTM_GETROUTE in the corpus carrying two
attributes. iproute_dump_filter writes RTA_TABLE first (:1726) then
RTA_OIF (:1731); a goip that emitted them in the other order would print
byte-identical text, and the gate is what makes that a failure.
UNGATED_CLEAN is therefore load-bearing for exactly one command again,
and that command is `-s link show`.
`neigh show dev` is the fifteenth and it is gated, on two measured runs
whose GOIP_PARITY lines were identical once pids and the live counters
below are normalized. Both reported `txns: ip=2 goip=2` and `control:
nl=2 stdout=0`, six datagrams and 162 bytes of stdout on all three sides.
It is the first command gated with a nonzero control count that did not
arrive with one of its own. Its nl=2 is the SAME two loci as `neigh
show`'s, for the same reason and on the same txn[0]: both send
ll_init_map's 0x01 link dump first, so both get live stats back. The
argument for gating it is therefore the one already made above for the
noisy four - D_control absorbs a control-explained locus before
Result.Findings exists, so `control: nl=2` sits next to PASS and a gate
has nothing to act on - and gating changes the verdict in exactly one
situation, a divergence D_control could not explain.
Gating it buys what no output comparison could, and the reason is the
opposite of `route show dev`'s. That selector moved a transaction; this
one adds nothing at all. `neigh show` and `neigh show dev` both measure
two transactions and six datagrams, and the ONLY difference between them
on the wire is eight bytes: an NDA_IFINDEX attribute on the second
request. There is no throwaway ll_link_get, because ll_init_map runs
BEFORE ll_name_to_index (ip/ipneigh.c:597 then :600), so the name
resolves out of the cache the dump just filled and ll_link_get is never
reached (lib/ll_map.c:354-359). Nothing in the replies records the
filter either - the kernel returns the same neighbors this topology
would have shown unfiltered. A goip that ignored `dev` entirely would
therefore print byte-identical text and send the right number of
datagrams, and only positional request equality could see it.
The OTHER way to get it wrong is caught, and loudly, but by the kernel
rather than by this harness: struct ndmsg has an ndm_ifindex field at
offset 4 and iproute2 leaves it zero, and under NETLINK_GET_STRICT_CHK -
which `ip` sets at ip/ip.c:312 and goip at internal/goip/source.go:93 -
neigh_valid_dump_req answers a nonzero ndm_ifindex with EINVAL and the
message "Invalid values in header for neighbor dump request"
(net/core/neighbour.c:2897-2901). This paragraph used to claim that
mistake was silent too. It is silent only on a socket without the option,
where the field is simply unread - so the loudness is a property of a
setsockopt made elsewhere, and the gate is still what makes the first
mistake fail.
`neigh show proxy` is the sixteenth command and the fifteenth gated one,
on two measured runs whose neigh_show_proxy lines were identical: `txns:
ip=2 goip=2` and `control: nl=2 stdout=0` both times, six datagrams and
58 bytes of stdout on all three sides. Its nl=2 is the SAME two loci as
`neigh show`'s and `neigh show dev`'s, on the same txn[0], for the same
reason - all three send ll_init_map's 0x01 link dump first, so all three
get live IFLA_STATS and IFLA_STATS64 back. It inherits that argument
rather than needing a new one.
The two runs were NOT identical overall, and the difference is worth
recording because it is the CONTROL_NOISY thesis being demonstrated
rather than undermined. GOIP_PARITY_CONTROL_NOISY was 14 and then 10,
entirely because `-s link show` measured nl=6 and then nl=2 - the
predicted permanently-noisy command sampling differently, as its own
paragraph above says it will. Every other command's control count was
the same on both runs. A total that moves while every gated command's
own count holds is exactly the shape that number should have.
Gating it buys something neither `dev` row does, and the reason is that
this selector changes the QUESTION rather than narrowing the answer.
net/core/neighbour.c:2955-2957 tests ndm_flags == NTF_PROXY - an
EQUALITY - and dispatches to pneigh_dump_table instead of
neigh_dump_table, so the two commands walk different tables and return
disjoint sets. A goip that dropped the byte would send a well-formed
request, receive a well-formed reply, and print the wrong table. Here
the stdout half would happen to catch it, because the two tables are
disjoint in this topology and 58 bytes is not 202 - but that is a
property of the topology, not of the comparison, and a topology with no
proxy entry and no regular one would make both sides empty and equal.
Only positional request equality sees the byte itself.
The OTHER way to get it wrong is loud, and again the kernel is what
makes it loud rather than this harness. Under NETLINK_GET_STRICT_CHK,
neigh_valid_dump_req rejects `ndm_flags & ~NTF_PROXY` with EINVAL and
the message "Invalid flags in header for neighbor dump request"
(net/core/neighbour.c:2903-2906), so a goip that or-ed NTF_PROXY into
another bit gets an error rather than the regular table back. Note what
that means for the equality above: the lenient fallthrough it describes
is unreachable on a socket with the option set, and both programs set it
- `ip` at ip/ip.c:312, goip at internal/goip/source.go:93.
One thing here must NEVER get an entry: ndm_flags itself, at
request:RTM_GETNEIGH offset 10. It is a request value, so the loader
would accept a suppression of it, and that is precisely the trap.
Suppressing it would mean goip asking the kernel for a different table
than `ip` did and the harness reporting parity. The version-skew entry
below is at the RTM_GETLINK ext-mask locus and nowhere near this one.
UNGATED_CLEAN goes back to being load-bearing for exactly one command,
and it is still `-s link show`. The paragraph above that says so was
briefly false while this command was compared but not yet gated.
THE FOUR `-d` COMMANDS ARE THE SEVENTEENTH THROUGH TWENTIETH, AND THEY
ARE THE SIXTEENTH THROUGH NINETEENTH GATED. `-d link show`, `-d addr
show`, `-d route show` and `-d neigh show` were written ungated,
measured twice that way, and only then gated and measured three times
more. That is the sequence every gated command above went through and
the reason UNGATED_CLEAN exists at all; the only difference is that
here it happened within one commit rather than across two. The
paragraphs below are in the order they were written, prediction before
measurement, and they are left that way on purpose: the predictions
were made before the first run and none had to be revised afterward.
Their request halves should be UNINTERESTING, and that is a prediction
worth writing down before the runs rather than after. show_details is
not one of the two variables iplink_filter_req reads
(ip/ipaddress.c:2017-2026) and it reaches nothing iproute_dump_filter
or ipneigh_dump_filter writes, so each of these four should send bytes
identical to its plain sibling. An L2 finding on a -d row is therefore
a goip bug rather than a discovery about iproute2.
Their stdout halves are where the content is, and they differ in KIND.
`-d link show` and `-d addr show` ADD tokens - sixteen per link, from
attributes the kernel was already sending and nothing was reading. `-d
route show` adds none: it UNSUPPRESSES four whose value is the default
(ip/iproute.c:828, :903, :909, :916), so what it tests is suppression
logic no plain golden can reach. `-d neigh show` changes nothing at
all, because ip/ipneigh.c does not contain the identifier - and that
row exists precisely because a goip which DROPPED -d would also change
nothing, so only a live `ip` given the same flag tells the two apart.
One thing to watch on `-d link show` specifically: nlmon0's promiscuity
is 1 inside a capture window and 0 outside it, because tcpdump holds a
packet socket on that interface. Both sides of a triple run inside the
window, so it should agree here - and if it ever does not, the cause is
a capture that started or stopped between the two rather than a
rendering bug. The offline test against the committed ip_link_n has to
substitute that one field for the same reason; see
internal/goip/goip_details_test.go.
WHAT THE TWO UNGATED RUNS MEASURED, which is the evidence this change
acts on.
-d link show    txns 1=1  control nl=0 stdout=0  1194 B x3
-d addr show    txns 2=2  control nl=0 stdout=0  1685 B x3 / 1687 B x3
-d route show   txns 2=2  control nl=0 stdout=0   507 B x3
-d neigh show   txns 2=2  control nl=2 stdout=0   575 B x3
Both runs' GOIP_PARITY lines were byte-identical to each other, twenty
PASS, UNGATED_CLEAN and CONTROL_NOISY 20 both times. Three of the four
cleared `nl=0 stdout=0` with nothing suppressed, which is the bar the
top of this file sets. `-d neigh show`'s nl=2 is the SAME two loci as
`neigh show`'s, `neigh show dev`'s and `neigh show proxy`'s, on the same
txn[0] and for the same reason - all four send ll_init_map's 0x01 link
dump first, so all four get live IFLA_STATS and IFLA_STATS64 back. It
inherits the argument those three already made rather than needing a
new one.
Two numbers worth reading rather than skipping. `-d addr show` measured
1685 bytes and then 1687, and that is not instability: the three SIDES
agreed exactly within each run, and the two bytes are the dummy's
link-local, which is derived from a MAC the kernel randomizes per boot.
A byte count that moves between boots and holds within one is the shape
a correct comparison has here. And `-d link show` measured nl=0 where
`-s link show` measured nl=2 then nl=6, which is the distinction those
two commands exist to make: -d asks for no counters, so its replies
carry none to be noisy about.
Those two runs were on trees differing by comments only, not on one
tree, so on their own they are advisory measurement rather than this
file's bar. They are also not evidence about the GATED build, for a
second and more basic reason: gating is the one edit that can alter a
verdict, since StatusWarn becomes StatusFail at
internal/goipparity/compare.go:198-204. So the rows were gated and the
tier was run again, three more times.
WHAT THE GATED RUNS MEASURED. Three of them, and the pair that counts
is the second and third: they ran back to back with no edit of any
kind between them, so they are two runs on ONE tree rather than on
trees differing by comments. The first gated run preceded two
test-file comment edits and is a third data point, not half the bar.
What the pair does NOT claim: that the tree they ran on is byte-equal
to the committed one. It cannot be - these paragraphs are the
difference, and a record of a run is always written after it. The
claim is the narrower and checkable one, that no edit separated the
two runs from EACH OTHER, so a difference between them would have
been the harness and not the tree.
-d link show    txns 1=1  control nl=0 stdout=0  1194 B x3
-d addr show    txns 2=2  control nl=0 stdout=0  1687 B x3
-d route show   txns 2=2  control nl=0 stdout=0   507 B x3
-d neigh show   txns 2=2  control nl=2 stdout=0   575 B x3
Both gated runs: twenty PASS, HYGIENE_PASS, UNGATED_CLEAN,
OVERALL_PASS, DRIVER_PASS. Their GOIP_PARITY line sets diff on exactly
one line, the CONTROL_NOISY total, 21 against 16. Across all FIVE runs
now on record - two ungated, three gated - these four rows' txn counts,
control counts and stdout byte counts are unchanged, with the single
exception noted below. That is what the gate rests on.
The CONTROL_NOISY total moved and nothing that matters moved with it,
which is the thesis rather than a crack in it. The whole 21-to-16 delta
is `neigh show proxy` going 6 to 2 and `-6 addr show` going 1 to 0 -
both pre-existing, both live-counter loci, neither a `-d` row. Every
one of the four `-d` rows measured the same control count in all five
runs: 0, 0, 0 and 2.
`-6 addr show` is worth a paragraph, and it CORRECTS one above. The
paragraph beginning "`addr show`, `-4 addr show`, `-6 addr show` and
`neigh show` complete the table" says two of those four are the
CONTROL_NOISY ones. That was true of the runs it was written from and
is no longer true of the set: `-6 addr show` measured nl=1 on two of
the three gated runs and nl=0 on the third, having measured nl=0 on
both ungated ones. The earlier paragraph is left as written, because
it is a record of what those runs measured, but the count of noisy
commands in it should be read as a sample rather than a property.
Its locus is reply:RTM_NEWLINK:IFLA_PROTINFO on ifindex 3, and that is
a DIFFERENT mechanism from every other noisy locus in this file. The
others are IFLA_STATS and IFLA_STATS64 hanging off a link dump. This
one is the v6 device's SNMP counters, nested inside IFLA_PROTINFO by
inet6_fill_ifinfo, and it is UNCONDITIONAL. inet6_fill_ifla6_attrs
does honor RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS (net/ipv6/addrconf.c:5850) - but
inet6_fill_ifinfo calls it with a hardcoded mask of 0 (:6110),
discarding whatever the client asked for. So no `ip -6 addr show` can
ever get a stats-free link dump, and this locus cannot be designed
away the way `-s link show`'s could be. It is moot in practice for a
second reason - rtnl_linkdump_req_filter_fn forwards filter_fn only
for AF_UNSPEC and AF_PACKET (lib/libnetlink.c:595), so an AF_INET6
dump carries no IFLA_EXT_MASK to be discarded - but the kernel side
is the one that would still hold if iproute2 started sending one.
Three boots quiet and two noisy is then just whether ICMPv6 traffic
landed between the two control captures.
It is also the clearest demonstration in the log of what gating a
control-noisy command actually means: `-6 addr show` is GATED, it
measured nl=1, and it reported PASS. D_control absorbs the locus
before Result.Findings exists, so the gate has nothing to act on. That
is the designed behavior observed rather than argued - and it is the
same argument this file makes for gating `-d neigh show` at nl=2, now
with a worked example attached.
One number moved among the `-d` rows and it is the one predicted to.
`-d addr show` measured 1685, 1687, 1686, 1687 and 1687 bytes over the
five boots, with the three SIDES agreeing exactly within every run.
The variable is the dummy's link-local, and the mechanism was computed
rather than assumed: the address is EUI-64 from a MAC the kernel
randomizes per boot, and leading-zero suppression in the four derived
hextets prints it as 25 characters about 82% of the time, 24 about 14%
and 23 about 3%. A spread of two characters across five boots is
exactly that distribution, and a count that holds across the three
sides within a run is what a correct comparison looks like here.
UNGATED_CLEAN is load-bearing for exactly one command again, and it is
still `-s link show` - the only command in the table that is compared
and not gated. That is now the whole of the ungated surface, so the
sentinel means precisely one thing: whether the permanently-noisy
command diverged in a way D_control could not explain.
THE FOUR `rule show` COMMANDS ARE THE TWENTY-FIRST THROUGH
TWENTY-FOURTH, AND THE TWENTIETH THROUGH TWENTY-THIRD GATED. `rule
show`, `-4 rule show`, `-6 rule show` and `-d rule show` were written
ungated and measured twice that way before being gated, which is the
sequence every command above went through.
WHAT THE TWO UNGATED RUNS MEASURED:
rule show          txns 1=1  control nl=0 stdout=0   742 B x3
-4 rule show       txns 1=1  control nl=0 stdout=0   742 B x3
-6 rule show       txns 1=1  control nl=0 stdout=0   131 B x3
-d rule show       txns 1=1  control nl=0 stdout=0  1002 B x3
All four cleared `nl=0 stdout=0` with NOTHING suppressed - not even a
suppressed finding - which is the bar the top of this file sets and the
one `link show` cleared. Both runs: twenty-four PASS, HYGIENE_PASS,
UNGATED_CLEAN, OVERALL_PASS. Their GOIP_PARITY line sets differ on
exactly two commands plus the CONTROL_NOISY total, 19 against 12, and
neither moving command is a rule row: `-4 addr show` went nl=6 to nl=2
and `neigh show proxy` nl=5 to nl=2, both pre-existing live-counter
loci. All four rule rows measured nl=0 in both runs.
Those two runs were on trees differing by a documentation edit, not on
one tree, so on their own they are the same grade of evidence as the
`-d` rows' ungated pair and are recorded the same way. The gated runs
below are the single-tree pair.
`rule show` is the FIRST command in the table whose ip side opens only
ONE socket. Every earlier row shows either a second pid in the `pids`
column - `ll_link_get`'s throwaway socket, once per relation iproute2
has to name - or an ll_init_map link dump ahead of the real request.
These four show `pids: ip=[N] goip=[M]`, one each, and txns 1=1 rather
than 2=2. That is not an optimization; it is that ip/iprule.c contains
no ll_init_map and cannot need one, because FRA_IIFNAME and FRA_OIFNAME
arrive as STRINGS and print_rule has no index to resolve. The harness
measuring it is what turns that source reading into an observation.
Gating them buys something no output comparison could, and the reason
is specific to this object: a rule dump request is 28 bytes with ZERO
attributes, and the kernel FORBIDS attributes on it -
fib_valid_dumprule_req errors with "Invalid data after header in fib
rule dump request" on any nonzero nlmsg_attrlen
(net/core/fib_rules.c:1278-1281). Meanwhile every `ip rule show`
selector - pref, from, to, iif, oif, table, fwmark - is applied
CLIENT-SIDE in filter_nlmsg (ip/iprule.c:98-243). So the request has
exactly one degree of freedom, the family byte, and that is the one
field fib_valid_dumprule_req does NOT validate (:1271-1276 checks
dst_len, src_len, tos, table, res1, res2, action and flags, and not
family). A goip that sent the wrong family byte would get a well-formed
reply to a different question, and on this topology `-6` returns four
rules where `-4` returns twenty, so it would print a plausible listing.
Only positional request equality sees the byte.
`-4 rule show` deserves its own line for the opposite reason: it should
be byte-identical to `rule show`, because iprule_list_flush_or_save

THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE EVIDENCE, AND THAT IS WORTH STATING PLAINLY

_note_version_skew: THE ENTRIES BELOW CITE COMMITS THAT ARE IN NO RELEASE, AND THE EVIDENCE IS
THE PINNED WIRE, NOT `git tag --contains`. A local iproute2 clone may have
fetched no tags at all, in which case --contains is empty for every commit
and proves nothing; ours has zero tags. What does prove it is the capture:
pkg/xtcpnl/testdata/7_1_4/dumps/ip_version records iproute2-7.1.0, and the
request bytes that ip put on the wire are the pre-commit behavior in every
case below. So these divergences do not exist against the pinned target
today and appear the moment the pin moves past them, which is the whole
reason `version-skew` requires an ip_version. Recording them now is cheaper
than rediscovering them as an unexplained red after a nixpkgs bump.
faceb326 has TWO independent loci and currently THREE entries, and the two
counts are not the same statement. The loci were measured rather than read
off the diffstat: flipping the render-time RenderQlenZero knob cannot
restore a clause the reply carries no attribute for, which is the proof
they are independent and that one entry would not cover both. The entry
count is larger because Entry.key() is command PLUS locus, and the
ioctl-fallback locus reaches two commands - `-6 addr show` and, found by a
live ungated run rather than predicted, `-s -6 addr show`. This sentence
said TWO entries until that third one landed; the hand-maintained count in
TestAllowlistCommitted caught the change and this prose did not, which is
the argument for the test row existing. See docs/netlink/coverage-status.md
and nix/upstream-pins.json, whose package_pins.iproute2 comment carries the
long form and correctly speaks of loci rather than entries.

entries.reason: MEASURED, not read off the source: the pinned 7.1.0 puts IFLA_EXT_MASK = 0x01 on this request, not 0x09. netlink_route_getneigh.pcap txn 0 is RTM_GETLINK with ifi_family = AF_UNSPEC and a single ext-mask attribute of 01000000, because 7.1.0's ll_init_map calls rtnl_linkdump_req(rth, AF_UNSPEC), which forwards RTEXT_FILTER_VF alone (lib/libnetlink.c). That is the one place in the corpus where the mask is not 0x09, and it is why this locus needs its own entry rather than sharing the link-show reasoning. TWO unreleased commits move it, in sequence: 7bd7f335 "ll_map: add RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS to ll_init_map()" (2026-04-28) rewrites the call as rtnl_linkdump_req_filter(rth, AF_UNSPEC, RTEXT_FILTER_VF | RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS), taking 0x01 to 0x09; then de91e928 "ll_map: add RTEXT_FILTER_NAME_ONLY to ll_link_get() and ll_init_map()" (2026-05-20) ors in RTEXT_FILTER_NAME_ONLY = (1 << 8), taking 0x09 to 0x109. A pin landing between them sees 0x09 and a pin past both sees 0x109, so one entry covers a range of values at one locus. The two bits do NOT behave alike on the reply side, and this entry used to claim they did. NAME_ONLY is newer than the kernel - linux/include/uapi/linux/rtnetlink.h stops at RTEXT_FILTER_MST (1 << 7) - so it exists only in iproute2's bundled header copy and this kernel ignores it. SKIP_STATS this kernel honors: net/core/rtnetlink.c:2155 gates rtnl_fill_stats on !(ext_filter_mask & RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS), and if_nlmsg_size drops the two attributes from its estimate at :1355 to match. The replies here demonstrably carry IFLA_STATS and IFLA_STATS64 today - they are the control noise this command reports on every run - so a pin past 7bd7f335 takes them away from ip and NOT from a goip still sending 0x01. That is a reply-side PRESENCE divergence, and D_control cannot absorb it: the two control captures would agree with each other and only goip would differ. This entry does not cover it and must not be widened to, because suppressing it would conceal a real difference in what the two programs asked the kernel for. The fix is the one named just below - every builder takes extMask from its caller, so the caller tracks the pin - and making it removes the request divergence and the reply divergence in the same edit. Until then this locus is request-only, and suppressing a request value is exactly what this allowlist may do. The locus ends `:dump` rather than `:ll_init_map` because that dump is the only NLM_F_DUMP RTM_GETLINK `neigh show` sends, and NLM_F_DUMP is what the comparator can actually see.

The same locus and the same two commits as the `neigh show` entry above, on a different command, and it needs its own row only because Entry.key() is command plus locus. `ip neigh show dev NAME` sends ll_init_map's link dump first and unconditionally - ip/ipneigh.c:597 calls it BEFORE the ll_name_to_index at :600 - so its txn 0 is byte-identical to the bare command's, IFLA_EXT_MASK = 01000000 and all: netlink_route_getneigh_dev.pcap and netlink_route_getneigh.pcap differ only on txn 1, by the eight bytes of NDA_IFINDEX. That identity is exactly why a shared entry is the tempting mistake. Widening the `neigh show` row to cover both, by dropping its command or matching a prefix, would mean a future divergence that appeared on only ONE of the two commands was suppressed on both, and the whole value of this selector is that its two requests are the only place the filter exists - nothing in the replies or the 162 bytes of stdout records it. So the duplication is the point, and the cost of the duplication is that 7bd7f335 and de91e928 will need both rows edited rather than one. Read the entry above for the derivation of 0x01 -> 0x09 -> 0x109, for why NAME_ONLY is inert on this kernel while SKIP_STATS is not, and for the reply-side consequence that neither row covers: this command is CONTROL_NOISY on IFLA_STATS and IFLA_STATS64 for precisely the reason that entry gives, measured nl=2 on both of the runs that earned its gate.

The third row at this locus, and the last one this object can produce. Same 0x01, same two commits, same Entry.key() reason for not sharing the rows above - read the `neigh show` entry for the 0x01 -> 0x09 -> 0x109 derivation and for the reply-side consequence no row here covers. What is worth saying separately is why a THIRD copy is not merely bookkeeping. `dev` narrows a dump the kernel already built; `proxy` makes the kernel walk a different table - net/core/neighbour.c:2955-2957 tests ndm_flags == NTF_PROXY, an EQUALITY, and dispatches to pneigh_dump_table instead of neigh_dump_table - so this command's replies are DISJOINT from the other two's rather than a subset of them. A shared entry would therefore suppress a future divergence on a command whose measured behavior it had never observed, which is a stronger objection than the one the `dev` row makes. MEASURED: netlink_route_getneigh_proxy.pcap txn 0 carries IFLA_EXT_MASK = 01000000, identical to the other two captures, and txn 1 is a bare twelve-byte ndmsg with 0x08 at offset 10 and zero everywhere else - one byte from the bare command's request, no attribute, nlparity_segment_test.go asserts the two bodies against each other rather than against a literal. One further thing does NOT need an entry and would be wrong to add one for: ndm_flags itself is a request field the comparator sees and must keep seeing, because it is the entire command. Suppressing a divergence there would mean goip asking for the wrong table and the harness calling it parity.

The second locus of de91e928: the single-get in ll_link_get, which fires once per relation iproute2 has to name while rendering. It is `:get` on the wire - NLM_F_REQUEST without NLM_F_DUMP - which is exactly what distinguishes it from the entry above. Unlike the ll_init_map locus, this one is already 0x09 at the pin - netlink_route_getlink_dev.pcap txn 0 is RTM_GETLINK with ifi_family = AF_UNSPEC, IFLA_EXT_MASK = 09000000 and IFLA_IFNAME, matching the pinned source exactly - `git show de91e928^:lib/ll_map.c` line 276 is the single line `__u32 filt_mask = RTEXT_FILTER_VF | RTEXT_FILTER_SKIP_STATS;`, where the tip spells the same variable across lines 276-277 because NAME_ONLY was appended to it. So 7bd7f335 does not touch it and only de91e928 does, taking 0x09 to 0x109: one commit and one bit here, against two commits and a 0x01 baseline there. That difference is exactly why these are two entries and not one - a run that exercises single-gets without an ll_init_map dump, or the reverse, must not have the other one silently allowlisted, and the two loci do not even hold the same pinned value to begin with.

iproute2 faceb326 "ip: drop unnecessary fallback to ioctl for tx queue length" (in no tag) rewrote print_queuelen from `if (qlen) print_int(...)` to an unconditional print_uint(...), so the released ip SUPPRESSES `qlen 0` while a post-faceb326 ip prints it. Three links in the committed dump carry IFLA_TXQLEN = 0 and their ip_link_n stanzas end at `group default ` with no qlen. goip implements the released behavior by default behind the named render.RenderQlenZero knob, with a test row on each side, so this is a flippable recorded fact rather than a silent choice. Stdout only: the netlink request and reply bytes are identical either way. The locus is spelled as internal/goipparity's stdout comparator derives it - `stdout:keyword:` plus the iproute2 output keyword - and not as a description of the cause, which is why this entry reads the same as the `-6 addr show` one below and is distinguished from it by `command`. It had been `stdout:link:qlen:IFLA_TXQLEN=0`, which no comparator emits; StdoutLoci() is the closed set and TestStdoutLociAreEnumerable checks this file against it.

faceb326's ioctl half reaching a SECOND command, and it is here because a measured run put it here rather than because the sweep predicted it. `-s -6 addr show` was added to the command table ungated, GOIP_PARITY_WARN addr_show_v6_stats reported `stdout value stdout:keyword:qlen: ip=1000 x2 goip=<absent>`, and that is the same absence the `-6 addr show` entry above describes: the AF_INET6 link dump is answered by inet6_dump_ifinfo, which emits no IFLA_TXQLEN at all, so 7.1.0's print_queuelen falls back to a SIOCGIFTXQLEN ioctl and prints `qlen 1000` for each link while a netlink-only goip prints nothing. `-s` has nothing to do with it - the two commands send byte-identical requests (TestTierAStatsRequestPairs measures zero differing bytes) and receive byte-identical replies, because inet6_fill_ifinfo calls inet6_fill_ifla6_attrs with ext_filter_mask hardcoded to 0 (net/ipv6/addrconf.c:6110). The skew was therefore fully predictable from the entry above, and it is still a separate entry rather than a widened one: Entry.key() is command plus locus, and keeping `-6 addr show` and `-s -6 addr show` distinct is what makes each a claim about a command that was actually run. Suppressing an absence rather than a value, for the second time in this file and the same reason.

faceb326's large half, and the reason its skew needs two entries rather than one. The commit also removed a SIOCGIFTXQLEN ioctl fallback in print_queuelen for when IFLA_TXQLEN is absent entirely. That path is unreachable on anything rtnl_dump_ifinfo answers - hence "unnecessary" upstream - but it is live on `ip -6 addr show`, whose link dump is answered by inet6_dump_ifinfo and carries no IFLA_TXQLEN at all. So 7.1.0 prints `qlen 1000` for lo there, from an ioctl, and goip prints nothing. Flipping RenderQlenZero cannot restore it: the knob chooses whether to print a zero, and there is no attribute here to print. goip will not issue an ioctl to match, because the comparator's subject is netlink and an ioctl is outside it. Two entries rather than one still, but now because the two commands differ rather than because the loci do: Entry.key() is command plus locus, so `stdout:keyword:qlen` on `link show` and on `-6 addr show` are distinct keys with distinct reasons, and neither widens to the other. It had been `stdout:addr6:qlen:IFLA_TXQLEN-absent`, which no comparator emits. This is the one place suppression covers an absence rather than a value; internal/goipparity/stdout.go's header argues why a rendered keyword is not a decoded attribute.
